site.name: modnest
site.intro: A mod is a plugin of function hooks that lives inside Claude Code: a hotkey, a pane, a status line, a voice. Each one here is a folder you load with a single flag, and each page says plainly what it does, what it needs and what it sends where.

mods.title: MYA
mods.tagline: Tap a key to talk to Claude Code, and hear it answer.
mods.summary: Hands-free voice for the terminal: dictate, translate in one key, hear MYA read Claude's answers aloud, and see a phone ring in a live band above your prompt when it is your turn.

does.text: A one-line MYA band above the prompt shows what it is doing: waiting, listening (with a moving level meter), thinking or speaking.

When Claude has finished and is waiting for you, a telephone rings in the band (and, if you turn it on, an old-fashioned bell rings). MYA also has a few lines of its own: a greeting at the start and a line when it did not hear you.
Tap, speak, tap again: your words are transcribed and sent to Claude.
Tap with the chord, speak, tap: your words are transcribed, translated (English by default) and sent.
Switch the hotkey off while you copy-paste elsewhere, and on again (also /mya off and /mya on). A Ctrl held a while, or used with a key, a click or the wheel, is never taken for a tap.

When you asked by voice, MYA reads Claude's answer aloud with a human-like Cartesia voice. Long answers are first condensed into a few spoken sentences; code and paths are not read out. Prefer something else? An ffmpeg robot effect, or a local machine voice (eSpeak NG, no key, no network), are one option away.
Tap while Claude is talking to cut it off and start your next question.

commands.name: /mya
commands.text: Fill the prompt with the dictation instead of sending it.

commands.name: /mya off
commands.text: Switch the Right Ctrl hotkey off.

requirements: Linux (not macOS or Windows). On X11 the hotkey is read with xinput; on Wayland it is three GNOME keyboard shortcuts that the included installer sets up

arecord and aplay (alsa-utils), xinput (X11 only) and Python 3. ffmpeg only for the optional robot effect and bell; libespeak-ng only for the optional machine voice. The helpers use the standard library only: nothing to pip install
A Deepgram API key for speech-to-text
A Cartesia API key to hear replies (not needed with the machine voice)
mods.installNote: Then set your keys in the plugin's options (/config, kept in secure storage) or in your shell environment as DEEPGRAM_API_KEY and CARTESIA_API_KEY. Never put keys in a file you commit.
options: Deepgram language code of what you say; also the speech language of replies
Names Deepgram should favour; common mishearings (like "I car") are corrected
Target language of the translate chord
Read answers aloud when the question was voiced
cartesia (human-like cloud voice) or machine (eSpeak NG, local)
Machine engine only: eSpeak NG voice and variant (fr+klatt, en+m3...)
Cartesia only: plain, robot (buzzing 90s computer) or soft (grit only)
Rhythm of the machine voice: words per minute and the pause between words
Play a telephone bell when it is your turn
Speaking speed from 0.5 (slow) to 2.0 (fast); lower it if a voice talks too fast
Cartesia voice id; empty uses MYA's original voice (Katie)
Show the MYA band above the prompt
ALSA capture device; auto prefers a USB microphone
X11 only (under Wayland change the shortcuts in GNOME keyboard settings). X11 keycodes: Right Ctrl, Space (translate), Right Shift (hotkey on/off); list yours with xmodmap -pke
A dictation key held longer than this is not a tap
Whether the hotkey is active when the session starts
privacy: Your microphone audio goes to Deepgram while you record.
The text of Claude's answer, or its condensed version, goes to Cartesia when replies are spoken. With the machine voice nothing is sent for speech.
Translating and condensing use a small haiku call through your own Claude Code session.

Under Wayland the hotkey helper reads no key at all: GNOME runs mya-key when its own shortcut is pressed, and only three words are accepted through a private socket. On X11 it reads every key and mouse-button event with xinput and keeps only Right Ctrl and its two chord keys; every other key is dropped on the spot, nothing is stored or written. Read bin/hotkey.py before enabling it.
limits: The chord's Space also reaches the terminal as Ctrl+Space.
Recording is manual: it ends when you tap the key again, or after three minutes.
Wayland: the one-command installer of the shortcuts is for GNOME; elsewhere bind any shortcut to bin/mya-key toggle, translate and lock yourself. Not tested on other desktops or distributions.
